title.narrative: Design and implementation of employment policies improved

description.narrative: Over the past decade, unemployment rates in Georgia have shown a steady decline, but remain high in international comparison. While the unemployment rate is higher for men than for women, women’s labour force participation remains much lower. This gender gap in labour force participation is pronounced for the age group 25–34 and in rural populations. Youth employment remains a pressing concern, with young people disproportionately affected by unemployment. Vulnerable segments of the population, including persons with disabilities, ethnic minorities and internally displaced persons (IDPs), continue to face barriers in accessing quality employment opportunities, exacerbating inequalities. These employment indicators point to the need for (i) measures to support population categories who are at higher risk of labour market exclusion (women, youth, and PwD), as well as (ii) innovative and evidence-based active labour market measures that address the specific labour market disadvantage of beneficiaries based on the individual characteristics that make them particularly vulnerable and likely to fall into long-term unemployment or inactivity. In 2024-2025, the ILO provides capacity support to constituents for the design and implementation of innovative active labour market measures targeting women and young people. Simultaneously, to enhance the effectiveness of public employment services, the ILO supports a training programme on active labour market measures to the staff of the recently created State Employment Support Agency. These efforts are aiming at increasing labour market participation of the population at higher risk of exclusion.
